newsitem.title: FINLAND: HARTWALL SAYS ORKLA DEAL NEUTRAL.
newsitem.headline: HARTWALL SAYS ORKLA DEAL NEUTRAL.

text.p: Finnish beverages maker Oy Hartwall Ab said in a statement on Friday that Norwegian food group Orkla ASA's acquisition of brewer Pripps-Ringnes AB would not have any impact on its operations.

"The deal in Pripps Ringnes shares will not have any impact on the businesses of Hartwall or BBH," Hartwall said, referring to Baltic Beverages Holding AB (BBH), which is 50-50 owned by itself and Pripps Ringnes.
Pripps Ringnes owns 20.5 percent of Hartwall shares (20.3 percent of votes).
Earlier, Orkla said it had agreed to take over the stake held by Swedish auto maker AB Volvo in Pripps-Ringnes.
Orkla said in a statement it valued Volvo's 55-percent share of the jointly-owned firm at four billion NOK. Orkla said it would take over Pripps-Ringnes with immediate effect.
Pripps-Ringnes will thereby become a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Orkla Group.
Pripps-Ringnes comprises the companies Pripps in Sweden, Ringnes in Norway and the 50-percent owned Baltic Beverages Holding (BBH), which has seven breweries in the Baltic States, Russia and Ukraine.

"The Nordic countries are the natural home market for Orkla's branded products," Orkla said. "The full takeover of Pripps-Ringnes confirms Orkla's position in the Nordic region and gives the Group a strong position in Eastern Europe. The takeover therefore strengthens the Group's branded products business," it said.
